steps.description: FP&A manager issues the budget calendar, central planning assumptions (inflation, FX, interest rates) and a quantified, re-runnable downside macro scenario. A drafting agent pulls macro feeds and generates a first-cut calendar and scenario from the prior-cycle template; the FP&A manager reviews, edits and is the named, dated author who issues the package. Output is dual-channel: a structured data feed for units with portal/ERP access, and an equally authoritative static document (PDF/spreadsheet) for offline submitters. If a data feed is stale or unavailable, the agent flags the gap rather than silently interpolating and the FP&A manager supplies the figure manually. The downside scenario remains a legible, inspectable artefact, not merely a parameter buried inside a model.
steps.name: Issue calendar and central planning assumptions

steps.description: CEO/CFO set top-down revenue, margin and cost targets as strategic allocation judgment, unchanged in substance from the baseline. An optional advisory analytics dashboard may surface historical performance and strategic-plan alignment, but it is decision support only and never an authoring actor; the CEO/CFO remain the sole accountable authors of the target, distinct from FP&A's assumption-issuance role in TS-01.
steps.name: Set top-down targets

steps.description: Business unit heads prepare and own revenue and volume plans. A forecast-drafting agent may produce a statistical baseline from historical actuals and pipeline data as a starting point, but the BU head reviews, overrides and submits the final number and must be able to explain and defend it; the agent's baseline and the final submission are both retained and diffed so material departures are visible. Offline-capable, template-based submission with validation remains a first-class path, not a deprecated exception, for units without forecasting-tool access; on connector failure the agent falls back to a prior-year template and logs the degraded mode without blocking the BU head.
steps.name: Revenue and volume plans

steps.description: Cost centre owners prepare and own cost centre and headcount budgets, kept as a distinct, separately accountable step from revenue planning and capex so that challenge in review can trace a number to a single owner. A cost-drafting agent may propose a baseline indexed to central assumptions and run-rate; the owner reviews and owns the submission, with offline spreadsheet-based submission remaining a legitimate path for locally-owned attrition/backfill judgment in offshore or thin-connectivity contexts.
steps.name: Cost centre and headcount budgets

steps.actor: Business unit heads; CFO / capital allocation committee (reviewer)
steps.description: Business unit heads submit capex requests. A deterministic validation agent enforces a hard completeness gate: no request above threshold may be submitted without an attached business case. Separately, every above-threshold request is routed to a named reviewer (CFO or capital allocation committee) who substantively reads and signs off the case before it proceeds to consolidation; the agent's pass/fail is not itself the approval. Any exception path is logged and attributable.
inputs: Business case for capex above threshold
steps.name: Capex requests

steps.description: Submissions are consolidated into a draft three-statement budget prepared on the same accounting basis as actuals. A consolidation agent automates aggregation, applies the version-pinned accounting policies and central FX assumptions used for actuals, and runs a deterministic three-statement reconciliation; for multi-entity groups it explicitly performs intercompany identification and elimination consistent with how actuals are consolidated. Any reconciliation break, policy deviation, or FX override halts the run and routes to a named FP&A analyst/controller, who certifies a discrete, evidenced 'reconciled' snapshot before the draft proceeds — recomputation may be frequent, but every snapshot that moves forward is explicitly certified, not merely live. A documented manual consolidation and tie-out procedure exists as a fallback when the platform is unavailable, using the same policy and FX inputs.
steps.name: Consolidate into draft P&L, balance sheet, cash flow

steps.description: The draft budget is reviewed and challenged in iterations with submitters by the FP&A manager and CFO. This remains a discrete, nameable, closeable negotiation step — not a standing exception queue — fed by an automated variance/exception-flagging agent that highlights the largest departures from target, prior year and the downside scenario to focus the conversation. Review is time-boxed to a defined number of rounds with an explicit non-convergence escalation path: specific line items that do not converge are kicked back to TS-03/TS-04/TS-05 for resubmission (not silently overridden by FP&A), and persistent non-convergence past the final round is escalated to the CFO for a logged, attributed override decision. An asynchronous, document-based challenge log is maintained alongside any live review sessions so participants without reliable bandwidth or synchronous access can take part.
steps.name: Review and challenge iterations

steps.description: The board approves the budget as a discrete, evidenced governance act that strictly precedes load-and-lock. The board pack presents the reconciliation certification, the downside scenario's treatment, and any unresolved or escalated challenges from TS-07 — not a sanitised summary — so that approval is informed, not ceremonial. An optional assistant may compile board materials, but the approval act itself is irreducibly human and is the recorded trigger condition for TS-09.
steps.name: Board approval

steps.description: The approved budget is loaded and immutably locked as the single version used by variance analysis. A load-and-lock mechanism is triggered only by a verified approval record — either a system-of-record approval signal or, where no such system is reachable, a signed-off manual document with a logged change history treated as an equally valid trigger — enforcing board-approval-before-lock architecturally, not merely by sequence. Before finalising the lock, a named FP&A analyst distinct from whoever executed the load independently confirms (via diff/hash or manual comparison) that the loaded artefact matches the board-approved artefact. Any later correction requires an explicit, logged unlock-relock action referencing the governing approval; silent post-lock edits are not permitted.
steps.name: Load and lock approved version
